confirm.text: Re-read directly from the source PDF. The form carries no OWL After Action Review section at all, so there is no close-out narrative to add context. Follow-up: confirm with Drake what the reach limitation was and whether an alternative testing method was available, and whether the crew being "under air" was verified independently.

2. Bobby Galindo 1099 — XTO, Northeast Scharbauer 1220H, Tarzan TX — air job 7:28 AM to 1:23 PM, job 36321. An 85 ppm H2S reading, recorded in the "What Went Well? Continued" narrative box rather than in a gas-reading field.

"Around 8ish this morning did the initial reading and it read 85 ppm of H2S. The crew wasn't working at this point, but did notify the MT and crew where H2S was present (tubing). Crew started their job around 10 and before they could work checked the tubing area for H2S and it was clear. No H2S was present. Notified MT. All breaks were clear of H2S. All safe to work."

Re-read directly from the source PDF. The account reads as correctly handled — crew not working at the time, MT notified, area reverified clear before work. Follow-up: a reading of this size belongs in a gas-reading field, not a free-text box, so it can be tracked. Worth confirming whether this was reported up at the time.
3. Alexander Clubb — SM Energy, NORM, Camille TB, Texon TX — air job, started 10/26 and ended 10/27 3:57 PM, job 36273. 60 ppm H2S and LEL on a vessel cleanout.
"Cleanout on vessel #3, got 60 ppm H2S on bleeder, when breaking open manway we were under air, after making break got 5 ppm H2S and OL lel, work continued for the duration of the job under air."

Re-read directly from the source PDF. The 10/26 day summary on the same job reads "Cleaned out vessel #4 BOOSTER, only gases that were picked up was LEL." Follow-up: confirm the readings were logged on the atmospheric testing log and reported to SM Energy.
4. Larry Jaramillo — XTO, Bend 45 #1, Midland TX — air job 6:40 AM to 10:11 AM, job 35555. A gas monitor found mounted outside its correct position on a third-party crew member.
"H2S minor was on the kill truck operator's hard hat, above the safe zone."

Re-read directly from the source PDF. "minor" appears to be a typo for monitor. The technician corrected it in the field — "Spoke with K/T operator and discussed the proper placement of his H2S monitor..." — and the Learn entry reads "Ensure everyone has on their proper PPE prior to work beginning...". This is good catch-and-correct work. See the stop-work section below for why the form's own selections do not reflect it.

"Trailer doors are broken in the back and jack stand was set too low and needs to be raised up higher"

Re-read directly from the source PDF. The field asks "If so what and who was notified?" and the second half is unanswered. Follow-up: establish who is now handling the rear doors and the jack stand, and whether trailer 139 should be in service in the meantime.

The 12/18 entries on bottles #4 and #5 would be nearly eight years old. Follow-up: confirm against the hydro interval Canon applies whether any of these bottles are out of test, and whether 2000 psi across the bank is a fill issue or a recording convention.

Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

None of today's 33 job forms selected "Stop work authority utilized". Five selected the routine pre-job item or the "Unsafe conditions" item. Per Kelby Hammer's 09/23 guidance these are reported as items needing the technician's confirmation, not as confirmed events — technicians may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose.
Four forms selected "Unsafe conditions" together with "Stop work authority was discussed" — discussed, not utilized. In each case the narrative is positive and names no specific unsafe condition:

Jeremy Norris — XTO, Massey Unit 4313H, job 36322. Narrative: "A great meeting between all to discuss the LMRAs and LSRAs as they pertain to this job and exactly what our ERP would be in case of emergency especially with it being a confined space location."
Ruben Rojo — XTO, University 178B 18H, job 36310. Re-read directly tonight. Narrative: "A reconnect on well head, team was thoroughly talked through on all LSRA's" — no condition named.
William "Jimmy" Cooper 1099 — XTO, Semple #1, job 35562. Narrative: "Teamwork".
William "Jimmy" Cooper 1099 — XTO, Bend 45 #1, job 35556. Narrative: "All hands participated in safety meeting".

A further five forms selected "Stop work authority was discussed" without "Unsafe conditions" — Bobby Galindo (36321), Cindy Smith 1099 (36355_2 and 36337_2), Bryan Medlin (36248) and Michael Jobe (36320). The same multi-select string recurs almost word for word across technicians and jobs, which points to a selection being carried forward rather than made fresh each time. That is the training point, not a finding against any individual.

One form runs the other way and is worth a closer look. Larry Jaramillo's Bend 45 #1 form (35555) describes a genuine condition — an H2S monitor worn above the safe zone on a kill truck operator's hard hat — and did not select "Unsafe conditions". His "What did we observe?" carries a single item, "Evaluation and discussion of life saving rules". This is the same inverse pattern seen with Jordan Lemmons on 09/26. The work itself was good: he spotted it, corrected it with the operator and wrote a sensible Learn entry. The form simply does not reflect what he did.

Dawson Drake's Junior Mint form (36358), carrying the no-atmospheric-testing statement in item 1, has no OWL section at all, so there is no selection either way and no close-out narrative. That absence is why item 1 is treated as real rather than as a selection artefact.

On repeat offenders: Nathan Contreras, who appeared on the stop-work confirmation list on 09/23 and again on 09/26, filed two job forms today (36316 and 36318) and selected no stop-work item on either. Michael Jobe, who selected "Unsafe conditions" twice in one day on 09/26, selected only "Stop work authority was discussed" today.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, never as text — so no statement in this report should be read as confirming any of those are current. The same applies to sensor calibration dates on the rig check forms, which are captured as photographs with no text value.

One further limitation specific to tonight: this review ran at 11:00 PM Central on 10/27, so the usual check of the following morning's mail for late arrivals could not be performed. Any form for 10/27 that lands tomorrow morning is not counted here, and some of the missing-documentation items above may be late rather than absent.

84 of 84 submissions read. The job board was available — the 10/27/2026 ArkLaTex and Permian Basin boards emailed by Blake Walton at 10:02 AM Central were used, and 72 manned board rows were checked for coverage (23 ETX, 49 WTX).
